#miRNA target gene AIC
```{r}
# Load libraries
library(multiMiR)        # miRNA target prediction
library(clusterProfiler) # Functional enrichment
library(org.Hs.eg.db)    # Human gene annotation
library(ggplot2)         # Visualization
library(enrichplot)      # Enrichment visualization
library(DOSE)            # Disease enrichment
library(ReactomePA)      # Reactome pathway analysis
library(STRINGdb)        # Protein-protein interaction network
```

#miRNA target gene AIC
```{r}
vers_table <- multimir_dbInfoVersions()
vers_table
db.tables = multimir_dbTables()
db.tables
db.info = multimir_dbInfo()
db.info
predicted_tables()
validated_tables()
diseasedrug_tables()


# Query multiMiR with all available sources
targets_hsa.miR.509.3p <- get_multimir(org = "hsa", mirna = "hsa-miR-509-3p", table = "validated")
targets_hsa.miR.377.3p <- get_multimir(org = "hsa", mirna = "hsa-miR-377-3p", table = "validated")
targets_hsa.miR.miR.378h <- get_multimir(org = "hsa", mirna = "hsa-miR-378h", table = "validated")


# Extract unique gene symbols
target_genes_hsa.miR.509.3p <- unique(targets_hsa.miR.509.3p@data$target_symbol)
target_genes_hsa.miR.377.3p  <- unique(targets_hsa.miR.377.3p@data$target_symbol)
target_genes_hsa.miR.378h  <- unique(targets_hsa.miR.miR.378h@data$target_symbol)


# Combine target genes from both miRNAs
target_genes <- unique(c(target_genes_hsa.miR.509.3p, target_genes_hsa.miR.377.3p, target_genes_hsa.miR.378h))

# View top target genes
head(target_genes)

# Convert to a data frame
target_genes_df <- data.frame(Gene_Symbol = target_genes)

head(target_genes_df)

# Save as CSV file
write.csv(target_genes_df, "target_genes_509_377_378h.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


#hallmark
```{r}
#load data of target genes
data = read.csv("target_genes_509_377_378h.csv")

##manual download database from msigdb
# Replace "path_to_file.gmt" with the path to your downloaded file
msigdb_hallmark <- read.gmt("MSigDB/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt")

# Perform enrichment analysis
hallmark_ORA <- enricher(gene = data$Gene_Symbol,
                               TERM2GENE = msigdb_hallmark,
                               pAdjustMethod = "BH", universe = NULL,
                               pvalueCutoff = 1,
                               qvalueCutoff = 1,
                               minGSSize = 20,
                               maxGSSize = 1000)

head(hallmark_ORA)

write.csv(hallmark_ORA, file = "hallmark_ORA.csv")

hallmark_ORA_plot <- dotplot(
  hallmark_ORA,
  x = "GeneRatio",
  color = "p.adjust",
  showCategory = 20,
  size = NULL,
  split = NULL,
  font.size = 8,
  title = "",
  label_format = 30,)

# Adjust size and save the plot
ggsave(filename = "hallmark_ORA_plot.png", plot = hallmark_ORA_plot, width = 8, height = 8)

print(hallmark_ORA_plot)
```

#PPI
```{r}
library(STRINGdb)
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)

# --- 1. Load and Initialize ---
target_genes <- read.csv("target_genes_509_377_378h.csv")

# Rename to match STRINGdb mapping expectation
de_results_string <- data.frame(
  gene = target_genes$Gene_Symbol,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

string_db <- STRINGdb$new(version = "11.5", species = 9606,
                           score_threshold = 700, input_directory = "")

# --- 2. Mapping and Handling Duplicates ---
mapped <- string_db$map(de_results_string, "gene", removeUnmappedRows = TRUE)

# Convert to standard data frame
mapped_df <- as.data.frame(mapped)
mapped_df <- mapped_df[!is.na(mapped_df$STRING_id) & mapped_df$STRING_id != "", ]

# Remove duplicate STRING_ids (keep first occurrence, no logFC to rank by)
mapped_unique <- mapped_df[!duplicated(mapped_df$STRING_id), ]

# Re-organize so STRING_id is the first column
mapped_final <- mapped_unique[, c("STRING_id", setdiff(names(mapped_unique), "STRING_id"))]
mapped_final$STRING_id <- as.character(mapped_final$STRING_id)

cat("Mapped genes:", nrow(mapped_final), "\n")

# --- 3. Build the Network ---
interactions <- string_db$get_interactions(mapped_final$STRING_id)

ppi_network <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = interactions,
  vertices = mapped_final,
  directed = FALSE
)
ppi_network <- simplify(ppi_network)

print(paste("Network built with", vcount(ppi_network), "nodes and",
            ecount(ppi_network), "edges."))

# --- 4. Hub Analysis ---
V(ppi_network)$Degree       <- degree(ppi_network)
V(ppi_network)$Betweenness  <- betweenness(ppi_network)
V(ppi_network)$Closeness    <- closeness(ppi_network)  # added extra metric

hub_table <- data.frame(
  STRING_ID   = V(ppi_network)$name,
  Gene        = V(ppi_network)$gene,
  Degree      = V(ppi_network)$Degree,
  Betweenness = V(ppi_network)$Betweenness,
  Closeness   = V(ppi_network)$Closeness
)

hub_table <- hub_table[order(-hub_table$Degree), ]

write.csv(hub_table, "hub_analysis_miRNA_targets.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Show top 10 hub genes
head(hub_table, 10)
```



```{r}
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Take top 50 hubs by degree ---
top_50_hubs <- hub_table$STRING_ID[1:50]
ppi_top_hubs <- induced_subgraph(ppi_network, vids = top_50_hubs)

# --- 2. Plot colored by Betweenness instead of logFC ---
gg_targets <- ggraph(ppi_top_hubs, layout = "nicely") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.2, color = "grey") +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = Betweenness, size = Degree)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = gene), repel = TRUE, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "darkred") +
  theme_graph() +
  labs(title = "Top 50 Hub Genes - miRNA Target PPI Network",
       color = "Betweenness",
       size = "Degree")

print(gg_targets)

# --- 3. Save ---
ggsave("PPI_miRNA_targets_Top50.png", gg_targets, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```


#metrics
```{r}
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# --- 1. Function to calculate metrics ---
calculate_hub_metrics <- function(g) {
  df <- data.frame(
    gene        = V(g)$gene,
    Degree      = degree(g),
    Betweenness = betweenness(g, normalized = TRUE),
    PageRank    = page_rank(g)$vector,
    Eigenvector = eigen_centrality(g)$vector
  )
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      z_Deg = scale(Degree),
      z_Bet = scale(Betweenness),
      z_Pag = scale(PageRank),
      z_Eig = scale(Eigenvector),
      Composite_Score = (z_Deg + z_Bet + z_Pag + z_Eig) / 4
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(Composite_Score)) %>%
    head(20)
  
  return(df)
}

# --- 2. Apply to miRNA target network ---
hub_data <- calculate_hub_metrics(ppi_network)

# --- 3. Save full hub metrics table ---
write.csv(hub_data, "hub_metrics_miRNA_targets.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# --- 4. Helper function for bar charts ---
make_hub_plot <- function(df, col_name, title, x_lab, fill_color) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(gene, Composite_Score), y = !!sym(col_name))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = fill_color, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", !!sym(col_name))),
              hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = x_lab) +
    theme(axis.line.y  = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          plot.title   = element_text(size = 10, face = "italic", hjust = 0.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .2)))
}

# --- 5. Create 5 individual plots ---
p1 <- make_hub_plot(hub_data, "Composite_Score", "Composite Hub Score",   "(mean z-score)",            "#FFCE44")
p2 <- make_hub_plot(hub_data, "Degree",          "Degree",                "(# direct interactions)",   "#6096BA")
p3 <- make_hub_plot(hub_data, "Betweenness",     "Betweenness Centrality","(bridge importance)",       "#D6824D")
p4 <- make_hub_plot(hub_data, "PageRank",        "PageRank",              "(network influence)",       "#5E7453")
p5 <- make_hub_plot(hub_data, "Eigenvector",     "Eigenvector Centrality","(hub-of-hubs score)",       "#8E5BB0")

# --- 6. Combine with patchwork ---
final_hub_plot <- (p1 | p2 | p3 | p4 | p5) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Hub Gene Analysis — miRNA Target Network (509-3p / 377-3p / 378h)",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold",
                                            hjust = 0.5, color = "#225577"))
  )

# --- 7. Print and Save ---
print(final_hub_plot)
ggsave("Hub_Gene_Analysis_miRNA_targets.png", final_hub_plot, width = 20, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

#miRNA-specific annotation on PPI network
```{r}
library(ggraph)
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)

# --- 1. Rebuild per-miRNA gene lists ---
gene_509  <- unique(targets_hsa.miR.509.3p@data$target_symbol)
gene_377  <- unique(targets_hsa.miR.377.3p@data$target_symbol)
gene_378h <- unique(targets_hsa.miR.miR.378h@data$target_symbol)

# --- 2. Assign category to each gene ---
all_genes <- data.frame(gene = unique(c(gene_509, gene_377, gene_378h)),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

all_genes$category <- case_when(
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_509  & all_genes$gene %in% gene_377  & all_genes$gene %in% gene_378h ~ "All 3",
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_509  & all_genes$gene %in% gene_377  ~ "509 & 377",
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_509  & all_genes$gene %in% gene_378h ~ "509 & 378h",
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_377  & all_genes$gene %in% gene_378h ~ "377 & 378h",
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_509  ~ "miR-509-3p only",
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_377  ~ "miR-377-3p only",
  all_genes$gene %in% gene_378h ~ "miR-378h only",
  TRUE ~ "Unknown"
)

# --- 3. Annotate vertices in top 50 hub subgraph ---
top_50_hubs <- hub_table$STRING_ID[1:50]
ppi_top50   <- induced_subgraph(ppi_network, vids = top_50_hubs)

# Match category to each node
node_categories <- all_genes$category[match(V(ppi_top50)$gene, all_genes$gene)]
node_categories[is.na(node_categories)] <- "Unknown"
V(ppi_top50)$category <- node_categories

# --- 4. Plot ---
category_colors <- c(
  "miR-509-3p only" = "#4E79A7",
  "miR-377-3p only" = "#F28E2B",
  "miR-378h only"   = "#59A14F",
  "509 & 377"       = "#B07AA1",
  "509 & 378h"      = "#76B7B2",
  "377 & 378h"      = "#FF9DA7",
  "All 3"           = "#E15759",
  "Unknown"         = "grey80"
)

gg_annotated <- ggraph(ppi_top50, layout = "nicely") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.2, color = "grey") +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = category, size = Degree)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = gene), repel = TRUE, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_color_manual(values = category_colors) +
  theme_graph() +
  labs(title = "Top 50 Hub Genes — Colored by miRNA Source",
       color = "miRNA Source",
       size  = "Degree")

print(gg_annotated)
ggsave("PPI_miRNA_annotated_Top50.png", gg_annotated, 
       width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

#select theme
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# ORA Dot Plot — miR-509-3p / miR-377-3p / miR-378h Target Genes
# Publication-quality figure for main manuscript
#
# Input files required (same directory as this script):
#   all_go_ORA.csv   — GO terms (BP + MF + CC)
#   all_cp.csv       — Canonical pathways (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, PID)
#   hallmark_ORA.csv — MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
#   all_tft.csv      — Transcription factor target gene sets
#
# Output:
#   ORA_dotplot_main.pdf  (vector, 8 x 10 in)
#   ORA_dotplot_main.png  (300 dpi, 8 x 10 in)
# =============================================================================

# ── 0. Load packages ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
library(tidyverse)   # ggplot2, dplyr, readr, forcats, stringr
library(scales)      # pretty_breaks, scientific
library(ggtext)      # element_markdown for rich text (optional)

# ── 1. Read input files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
go_df       <- read_csv("all_go_ORA.csv",      show_col_types = FALSE)
cp_df       <- read_csv("all_cp.csv",           show_col_types = FALSE)
hallmark_df <- read_csv("hallmark_ORA.csv",     show_col_types = FALSE)
tft_df      <- read_csv("all_tft.csv",          show_col_types = FALSE)

# Tag each data frame with a source database label (for annotation)
go_df       <- go_df       %>% mutate(Source_DB = "GO")
cp_df       <- cp_df       %>% mutate(Source_DB = "CP")
hallmark_df <- hallmark_df %>% mutate(Source_DB = "Hallmark")
tft_df      <- tft_df      %>% mutate(Source_DB = "TFT")

# Combine all into one master data frame
all_ora <- bind_rows(go_df, cp_df, hallmark_df, tft_df)

# ── 2. Define curated 18 terms ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Theme order controls top-to-bottom facet ordering
# Term order within theme is controlled later by FoldEnrichment

curated <- tribble(
  ~Description,                                                              ~Display_Label,                      ~Theme,                    ~DB_label,
  "GOBP_CHROMATIN_REMODELING",                                               "Chromatin Remodeling",               "Epigenetic Reprogramming", "GO-BP",
  "GOBP_CHROMATIN_ORGANIZATION",                                             "Chromatin Organization",             "Epigenetic Reprogramming", "GO-BP",
  "GOMF_HISTONE_MODIFYING_ACTIVITY",                                         "Histone Modifying Activity",         "Epigenetic Reprogramming", "GO-MF",
  "GOBP_MIRNA_METABOLIC_PROCESS",                                            "miRNA Metabolic Process",            "miRNA Feedback Loop",      "GO-BP",
  "KEGG_PATHWAYS_IN_CANCER",                                                 "Pathways in Cancer",                 "Oncogenic Signaling",      "KEGG",
  "REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_RECEPTOR_TYROSINE_KINASES",                         "RTK Signaling",                      "Oncogenic Signaling",      "Reactome",
  "REACTOME_PTEN_REGULATION",                                                "PTEN Regulation",                    "Oncogenic Signaling",      "Reactome",
  "REACTOME_KEAP1_NFE2L2_PATHWAY",                                           "KEAP1\u2013NRF2 Pathway",            "Stress Resistance",        "Reactome",
  "HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS",                                                      "Apoptosis",                          "Cell Survival",            "Hallmark",
  "HALLMARK_PROTEIN_SECRETION",                                              "Protein Secretion",                  "Cell Survival",            "Hallmark",
  "WP_VEGFAVEGFR2_SIGNALING",                                                "VEGFA\u2013VEGFR2 Signaling",        "Angiogenesis & Invasion",  "WikiPathways",
  "WP_EPITHELIAL_TO_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION_IN_COLORECTAL_CANCER",            "Epithelial\u2013Mesenchymal Transition", "Angiogenesis & Invasion", "WikiPathways",
  "REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_TGFB_FAMILY_MEMBERS",                              "TGF-\u03b2 Signaling",              "Immune Evasion",           "Reactome",
  "GOBP_MYELOID_CELL_HOMEOSTASIS",                                           "Myeloid Cell Homeostasis",           "Immune Evasion",           "GO-BP",
  "GCCATNTTG_YY1_Q6",                                                        "YY1 Target Genes",                   "TF Network",               "TFT",
  "SOX5_01",                                                                 "SOX5 Target Genes",                  "TF Network",               "TFT",
  "GGGNNTTTCC_NFKB_Q6_01",                                                   "NF-\u03baB Target Genes",            "TF Network",               "TFT",
  "STAT3_02",                                                                "STAT3 Target Genes",                 "TF Network",               "TFT"
)

# ── 3. Join curated list with actual ORA values ───────────────────────────────
plot_df <- curated %>%
  left_join(
    all_ora %>% select(Description, FoldEnrichment, p.adjust, Count, GeneRatio),
    by = "Description"
  ) %>%
  # Parse GeneRatio string (e.g. "52/923") to numeric
  mutate(
    GeneRatio_num = map_dbl(GeneRatio, ~ {
      parts <- str_split(.x, "/")[[1]]
      as.numeric(parts[1]) / as.numeric(parts[2])
    }),
    neg_log10_padj = -log10(p.adjust)
  )

# Verify all 18 terms were matched
if (any(is.na(plot_df$FoldEnrichment))) {
  warning("Some terms not matched — check Description strings:")
  print(plot_df %>% filter(is.na(FoldEnrichment)) %>% select(Description, Display_Label))
}

# ── 4. Set factor levels for correct ordering ─────────────────────────────────

# Theme order (top → bottom in plot)
theme_order <- c(
  "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  "miRNA Feedback Loop",
  "Oncogenic Signaling",
  "Stress Resistance",
  "Cell Survival",
  "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  "Immune Evasion",
  "TF Network"
)

# Within each theme: order terms by FoldEnrichment (highest at top of group)
plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(Theme = factor(Theme, levels = rev(theme_order))) %>%
  group_by(Theme) %>%
  arrange(Theme, FoldEnrichment) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Display_Label = factor(Display_Label, levels = unique(Display_Label)))

# ── 5. Colour palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Strip background colours for each theme
theme_colours <- c(
  "Epigenetic Reprogramming" = "#7B4F9E",
  "miRNA Feedback Loop"      = "#C975B0",
  "Oncogenic Signaling"      = "#D62728",
  "Stress Resistance"        = "#FF7F0E",
  "Cell Survival"            = "#8B8B00",
  "Angiogenesis & Invasion"  = "#17BECF",
  "Immune Evasion"           = "#2CA02C",
  "TF Network"               = "#1F77B4"
)

# FDR colour ramp: light yellow → orange → dark red
fdr_colours <- c("#FFF5B0", "#FDB462", "#E31A1C")

# ── 6. Build the dot plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = FoldEnrichment, y = Display_Label)) +

  # Reference line at FE = 1
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.0,
             linetype   = "dashed",
             colour     = "grey55",
             linewidth  = 0.5) +

  # Dots: size = gene count, colour = -log10(FDR)
  geom_point(aes(size  = Count,
                 colour = neg_log10_padj),
             alpha = 0.92) +

  # DB source label to the right of each dot
  geom_text(aes(x     = max(plot_df$FoldEnrichment, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.18,
                label = DB_label),
            hjust  = 0,
            size   = 2.8,
            colour = "grey45",
            fontface = "italic") +

  # Facet by Theme (free y so each group only shows its own terms)
  facet_grid(Theme ~ .,
             scales = "free_y",
             space  = "free_y",
             switch = "y") +          # strip on LEFT side

  # Colour scale for FDR
  scale_colour_gradientn(
    colours = fdr_colours,
    name    = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
    guide   = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top",
      barwidth       = unit(5, "cm"),
      barheight      = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      frame.colour   = "grey50"
    )
  ) +

  # Size scale for gene count
  scale_size_continuous(
    name   = "Gene count",
    range  = c(3, 10),
    breaks = c(18, 25, 40, 61, 93),
    guide  = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      override.aes   = list(colour = "grey40")
    )
  ) +

  # X axis
  scale_x_continuous(
    name   = "Fold Enrichment",
    limits = c(1.0, max(plot_df$FoldEnrichment, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.9),
    breaks = pretty_breaks(n = 5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))
  ) +

  # Y axis label
  scale_y_discrete(name = NULL) +

  # Labels
  labs(
    title    = "ORA \u2014 miR-509-3p / miR-377-3p / miR-378h Target Genes",
    subtitle = "18 representative terms across 8 biological themes"
  ) +

  # Base theme
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    # Title
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "grey35", hjust = 0,
                                       margin = margin(b = 8)),

    # Facet strips (LEFT side, coloured by theme)
    strip.placement    = "outside",
    strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = "grey70"),
    strip.text.y.left  = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5,
                                       size = 8.5, face = "bold",
                                       colour = "white",
                                       margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4)),

    # Panel
    panel.border       = element_rect(colour = "grey75", fill = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey88", linetype = "dotted"),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_line(colour = "grey93", linetype = "dotted"),
    panel.spacing      = unit(0.25, "lines"),

    # Axis
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title.x       = element_text(size = 10, margin = margin(t = 6)),

    # Legend
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    legend.box         = "horizontal",
    legend.title       = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 8.5),
    legend.margin      = margin(t = 4),
    legend.box.margin  = margin(t = 2),

    # Extra right margin to fit DB labels
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 8, r = 60, b = 8, l = 8)
  ) +

  # Allow geom_text labels to extend beyond panel boundary
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

# ── 7. Apply theme-specific strip colours ─────────────────────────────────────
# ggplot2 does not natively support per-facet strip colours in facet_grid.
# We use a grob-level hack after building the plot.
# Alternative: use ggh4x::facet_grid2() if available.

apply_strip_colours <- function(gg_plot, theme_col_map) {
  library(grid)
  gt  <- ggplotGrob(gg_plot)
  # Find strip grobs on the left (y strips from facet_grid with switch="y")
  strip_idx <- which(grepl("strip-l", gt$layout$name))
  # Theme order in the grob (bottom to top because facet levels are reversed)
  themes_in_plot <- rev(levels(plot_df$Theme))
  for (i in seq_along(strip_idx)) {
    theme_name <- themes_in_plot[i]
    if (!is.null(theme_col_map[[theme_name]])) {
      strip_grob <- gt$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]]
      # Set the background rectangle colour
      strip_grob$grobs[[1]]$children[[1]]$gp$fill <- theme_col_map[[theme_name]]
      # Set the text colour to white
      strip_grob$grobs[[1]]$children[[2]]$gp$col  <- "white"
      gt$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]] <- strip_grob
    }
  }
  return(gt)
}

# ── 8. Save output ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Save plain ggplot first (works without grob manipulation if ggh4x absent)
ggsave("ORA_dotplot_main.pdf",
       plot   = p,
       width  = 8,
       height = 10,
       units  = "in",
       device = cairo_pdf)

ggsave("ORA_dotplot_main.png",
       plot   = p,
       width  = 8,
       height = 10,
       units  = "in",
       dpi    = 300,
       bg     = "white")

# Then attempt to apply per-strip colours and save a coloured version
tryCatch({
  gt_coloured <- apply_strip_colours(p, theme_colours)

  pdf("ORA_dotplot_main_coloured.pdf", width = 8, height = 10)
  grid::grid.draw(gt_coloured)
  dev.off()

  png("ORA_dotplot_main_coloured.png",
      width  = 8,  height = 10,
      units  = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
  grid::grid.draw(gt_coloured)
  dev.off()

  message("Coloured strip version saved successfully.")
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Strip colour grob edit failed — plain version already saved.")
  message("To get per-facet strip colours, install ggh4x and use facet_grid2().")
  message("Error: ", conditionMessage(e))
})

message("Done. Output files:")
message("  ORA_dotplot_main.pdf / .png         — base version")
message("  ORA_dotplot_main_coloured.pdf / .png — with theme strip colours")

# ── 9. Optional: ggh4x version (cleaner strip colours) ───────────────────────
# Uncomment this block if you have ggh4x installed:
#
# library(ggh4x)
#
# strip_designs <- strip_themed(
#   background_y = elem_list_rect(
#     fill = unname(theme_colours[theme_order])
#   ),
#   text_y = elem_list_text(colour = "white", face = "bold", angle = 0)
# )
#
# p_ggh4x <- p +
#   facet_grid2(Theme ~ .,
#               scales  = "free_y",
#               space   = "free_y",
#               switch  = "y",
#               strip   = strip_designs)
#
# ggsave("ORA_dotplot_ggh4x.pdf", p_ggh4x, width=8, height=10, device=cairo_pdf)
# ggsave("ORA_dotplot_ggh4x.png", p_ggh4x, width=8, height=10, dpi=300, bg="white")
```

#plot top 50 of each them
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# ORA 4-Panel Dot Plot — miR-509-3p / miR-377-3p / miR-378h
# Separate panels for GO, Canonical Pathways, Hallmark, and TFT
# Publication-quality figure for main or supplementary manuscript
#
# Input files (place in same directory as this script):
#   all_go_ORA.csv        GO terms (BP + MF + CC combined)
#   all_cp.csv            Canonical pathways (KEGG, Reactome, WikiPathways, PID)
#   hallmark_ORA.csv      MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
#   all_tft.csv           Transcription factor target gene sets
#
# Outputs:
#   ORA_4panel_dotplot.pdf    (vector, 20 x 28 in combined)
#   ORA_4panel_dotplot.png    (300 dpi)
#   ORA_GO_panel.pdf          Individual GO panel
#   ORA_CP_panel.pdf          Individual CP panel
#   ORA_TFT_panel.pdf         Individual TFT panel
#   ORA_Hallmark_panel.pdf    Individual Hallmark panel
# =============================================================================

# ── 0. Packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)   # combine panels: install.packages("patchwork")
library(ggtext)      # rich text labels: install.packages("ggtext")

# ── 1. Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
go_df       <- read_csv("all_go_ORA.csv",   show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(DB = "GO")
cp_df       <- read_csv("all_cp.csv",        show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(DB = "CP")
hallmark_df <- read_csv("hallmark_ORA.csv",  show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(DB = "Hallmark")
tft_df      <- read_csv("all_tft.csv",       show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(DB = "TFT")

# ── 2. Parse GeneRatio to numeric ─────────────────────────────────────────────
parse_ratio <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      GeneRatio_num = map_dbl(GeneRatio, ~ {
        x <- str_split(.x, "/")[[1]]
        as.numeric(x[1]) / as.numeric(x[2])
      }),
      neg_log10_padj = -log10(p.adjust)
    )
}

go_df       <- parse_ratio(go_df)
cp_df       <- parse_ratio(cp_df)
hallmark_df <- parse_ratio(hallmark_df)
tft_df      <- parse_ratio(tft_df)

# ── 3. Theme assignments ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each term is assigned to a biological theme.
# Terms NOT assigned here will be labelled "Other" and excluded from panels.

go_themes <- c(
  # Epigenetic Reprogramming
  GOBP_CHROMATIN_ORGANIZATION                                         = "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  GOBP_CHROMATIN_REMODELING                                           = "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  GOMF_CHROMATIN_BINDING                                              = "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  GOMF_HISTONE_MODIFYING_ACTIVITY                                     = "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  GOBP_EPIGENETIC_REGULATION_OF_GENE_EXPRESSION                       = "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  GOCC_TRANSCRIPTION_REGULATOR_COMPLEX                                = "Epigenetic Reprogramming",
  # Transcription & Gene Regulation
  GOMF_TRANSCRIPTION_FACTOR_BINDING                                   = "Transcription Regulation",
  GOMF_DNA_BINDING_TRANSCRIPTION_FACTOR_BINDING                       = "Transcription Regulation",
  GOMF_RNA_POLYMERASE_II_SPECIFIC_DNA_BINDING_TRANSCRIPTION_FACTOR_BINDI = "Transcription Regulation",
  GOMF_TRANSCRIPTION_COREGULATOR_ACTIVITY                             = "Transcription Regulation",
  GOCC_NUCLEAR_BODY                                                   = "Transcription Regulation",
  # miRNA Biology
  GOBP_MIRNA_METABOLIC_PROCESS                                        = "miRNA Biology",
  GOBP_MIRNA_TRANSCRIPTION                                            = "miRNA Biology",
  GOBP_REGULATION_OF_MIRNA_METABOLIC_PROCESS                         = "miRNA Biology",
  # Angiogenesis & Invasion
  GOBP_VASCULATURE_DEVELOPMENT                                        = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_TUBE_MORPHOGENESIS                                             = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_BLOOD_VESSEL_MORPHOGENESIS                                     = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_REGULATION_OF_CELL_PROJECTION_ORGANIZATION                    = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_POSITIVE_REGULATION_OF_CELL_PROJECTION_ORGANIZATION           = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_CELL_JUNCTION_ORGANIZATION                                     = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_CELL_PROJECTION_MORPHOGENESIS                                  = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  GOBP_REGULATION_OF_ANATOMICAL_STRUCTURE_MORPHOGENESIS              = "Angiogenesis & Invasion",
  # Growth & Proliferation
  GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_GROWTH_FACTOR                                      = "Growth & Proliferation",
  GOBP_REGULATION_OF_GROWTH                                           = "Growth & Proliferation",
  GOBP_REGULATION_OF_ORGAN_GROWTH                                     = "Growth & Proliferation",
  GOBP_DEVELOPMENTAL_GROWTH                                           = "Growth & Proliferation",

# ── 4. Apply theme assignments and filter ─────────────────────────────────────
assign_and_filter <- function(df, theme_vec, top_n = 50, padj_cut = 0.05) {
  df %>%
    filter(p.adjust < padj_cut) %>%
    arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_n) %>%
    mutate(Theme = theme_vec[Description]) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Theme))   # remove unassigned terms
}

go_plot_df       <- assign_and_filter(go_df,       go_themes,       top_n = 50)

hallmark_plot_df <- assign_and_filter(hallmark_df,  hallmark_themes, top_n = 50)
tft_plot_df      <- assign_and_filter(tft_df,       tft_themes,      top_n = 50)

cat("  CP:      ", nrow(cp_plot_df),       "\n")
cat("  Hallmark:", nrow(hallmark_plot_df), "\n")
cat("  TFT:     ", nrow(tft_plot_df),      "\n")

# ── 5. Clean up display labels ────────────────────────────────────────────────
clean_label <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_remove("^(GOBP|GOMF|GOCC|KEGG|REACTOME|WP|PID|HALLMARK)_") %>%
    str_replace_all("_", " ") %>%
    str_to_title() %>%
    str_trunc(55, ellipsis = "…")
}

add_display_label <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(Display_Label = clean_label(Description))
}

go_plot_df       <- add_display_label(go_plot_df)
cp_plot_df       <- add_display_label(cp_plot_df)
hallmark_plot_df <- add_display_label(hallmark_plot_df)

           str_replace_all("_TARGET_GENES", " targets") %>%

           str_to_title() %>%
           str_trunc(50, ellipsis = "…"))

# ── 6. Set factor levels (within-theme by FoldEnrichment, themes by order) ───
order_terms <- function(df, theme_order) {
  df %>%
    mutate(Theme = factor(Theme, levels = rev(theme_order))) %>%
    group_by(Theme) %>%
    arrange(Theme, FoldEnrichment) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(Display_Label = factor(Display_Label, levels = unique(Display_Label)))
}

# ── 8. Core plotting function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
make_dotplot <- function(df, title_label, strip_col_map,
                         x_max = NULL, x_breaks = NULL) {

  if (is.null(x_max))    x_max    <- max(df$FoldEnrichment, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05
  if (is.null(x_breaks)) x_breaks <- pretty_breaks(n = 4)

  n_terms  <- nrow(df)
  dot_max  <- max(df$Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  dot_min  <- min(df$Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  fdr_max  <- max(df$neg_log10_padj, na.rm = TRUE)

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = FoldEnrichment, y = Display_Label)) +

    # Reference line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.0, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.45) +

    # Dots
    geom_point(aes(size = Count, colour = neg_log10_padj),
               alpha = 0.90) +

    # Facet
    facet_grid(Theme ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +

    # Colour: FDR
    scale_colour_gradientn(
      colours  = fdr_colours,
      name     = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
      limits   = c(0, fdr_max),
      guide    = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        barwidth  = unit(4.5, "cm"),
        barheight = unit(0.4, "cm"),
        frame.colour = "grey50"
      )
    ) +

    # Size: gene count
    scale_size_continuous(
      name  = "Gene count",
      range = c(2.5, 9),
      guide = guide_legend(
        title.position = "top",
        override.aes   = list(colour = "grey40"),
        nrow = 1
      )
    ) +

    # X axis
    scale_x_continuous(
      name   = "Fold Enrichment",
      limits = c(0.9, x_max),
      breaks = x_breaks,
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.05))
    ) +

    scale_y_discrete(name = NULL) +

    labs(title = title_label) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 10.5) +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12,
                                         margin = margin(b = 4)),
      strip.placement    = "outside",
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey30", colour = NA),
      strip.text.y.left  = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 8,
                                         face = "bold", colour = "white",
                                         margin = margin(l = 3, r = 3)),
      panel.border       = element_rect(colour = "grey70", fill = NA,
                                         linewidth = 0.5),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey88", linetype = "dotted",
                                         linewidth = 0.4),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing      = unit(0.2, "lines"),
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "black"),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.title.x       = element_text(size = 9.5, margin = margin(t = 5)),
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.box         = "horizontal",
      legend.title       = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.text        = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.margin      = margin(t = 2),
      plot.margin        = margin(t = 6, r = 10, b = 4, l = 4)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

  return(p)
}

# ── 9. Build all 4 panels ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
p_go <- make_dotplot(go_plot_df,       
                     "Gene Ontology (BP + MF + CC)",  
                     go_strip_cols)

p_cp <- make_dotplot(cp_plot_df,       
                     "Canonical Pathways (KEGG / Reactome / WikiPathways / PID)",  
                     cp_strip_cols)

p_hallmark <- make_dotplot(hallmark_plot_df,  
                           "MSigDB Hallmark Gene Sets",  
                           hallmark_strip_cols)

p_tft <- make_dotplot(tft_plot_df,     
                      "Transcription Factor Targets (TFT)",  
                      tft_strip_cols)

# ── 10. Apply per-strip colours via grob editing ─────────────────────────────
apply_strip_colours <- function(p, strip_col_map) {
  library(grid)
  gt         <- ggplotGrob(p)
  strip_idx  <- which(grepl("^strip-l", gt$layout$name))
  # theme levels run bottom→top in grob order, but factor levels are reversed
  # so we need to map carefully
  theme_levels <- levels(p$data$Theme)  # already reversed (bottom=1)

  for (i in seq_along(strip_idx)) {
    # grob strips go top→bottom on page, so index from end
    theme_name <- theme_levels[length(theme_levels) - i + 1]
    col <- strip_col_map[[theme_name]]
    if (!is.null(col)) {
      strip_grob <- gt$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]]
      # background rect
      strip_grob$grobs[[1]]$children[[1]]$gp$fill <- col
      # text colour → white
      strip_grob$grobs[[1]]$children[[2]]$gp$col  <- "white"
      gt$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]] <- strip_grob
    }
  }
  return(gt)
}

# ── 11. Save individual panels ────────────────────────────────────────────────
save_panel <- function(p, strip_col_map, filename_base,
                       w = 9, h_per_term = 0.28, h_min = 4) {

  n     <- nrow(p$data)
  h     <- max(h_min, n * h_per_term + 2.5)

  # Plain version (always works)
  ggsave(paste0(filename_base, ".pdf"), p,
         width = w, height = h, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(paste0(filename_base, ".png"), p,
         width = w, height = h, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")

  # Coloured strip version (grob hack)
  tryCatch({
    gt <- apply_strip_colours(p, strip_col_map)
    pdf(paste0(filename_base, "_coloured.pdf"), width = w, height = h)
    grid::grid.draw(gt); dev.off()
    png(paste0(filename_base, "_coloured.png"),
        width = w, height = h, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
    grid::grid.draw(gt); dev.off()
    message("  Coloured strips saved: ", filename_base)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("  Strip colour edit failed for ", filename_base, ": ", e$message)
  })
}

message("Saving GO panel...")
save_panel(p_go,       go_strip_cols,       "ORA_GO_panel")

message("Saving CP panel...")
save_panel(p_cp,       cp_strip_cols,       "ORA_CP_panel")

message("Saving Hallmark panel...")
save_panel(p_hallmark, hallmark_strip_cols, "ORA_Hallmark_panel", h_min = 3)

message("Saving TFT panel...")
save_panel(p_tft,      tft_strip_cols,      "ORA_TFT_panel")

# ── 12. Combined 4-panel figure with patchwork ───────────────────────────────
# GO + CP side by side (top row), TFT + Hallmark (bottom row)
message("Saving combined 4-panel figure...")

combined <- (p_go | p_cp) / (p_tft | p_hallmark) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Over-Representation Analysis \u2014 miR-509-3p / miR-377-3p / miR-378h Target Genes",
    subtitle = "Top terms grouped by biological theme across four gene set databases",
    caption  = paste0("FDR < 0.05; top 50 terms shown per database after exclusion of",
                      " off-target (neuronal/developmental) terms.\n",
                      "Dot size = gene count. Colour = \u2212log\u2081\u2080(FDR)."),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30", hjust = 0),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8,  colour = "grey50", hjust = 0)
    )
  )

ggsave("ORA_4panel_dotplot.pdf", combined,
       width = 20, height = 28, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave("ORA_4panel_dotplot.png", combined,
       width = 20, height = 28, units = "in", dpi = 200, bg = "white")

message("\nAll done! Files saved:")
message("  ORA_GO_panel.pdf / .png / _coloured versions")
message("  ORA_CP_panel.pdf / .png / _coloured versions")
message("  ORA_TFT_panel.pdf / .png / _coloured versions")
message("  ORA_Hallmark_panel.pdf / .png / _coloured versions")
message("  ORA_4panel_dotplot.pdf / .png  (combined)")

# ── 13. Optional: ggh4x for cleaner strip colours ────────────────────────────
# If you install ggh4x, replace facet_grid() with facet_grid2() + strip_themed()
# inside make_dotplot(). Example:
#
# library(ggh4x)
# strip_designs <- strip_themed(
#   background_y = elem_list_rect(fill = unname(strip_col_map[theme_order])),
#   text_y       = elem_list_text(colour = "white", face = "bold", angle = 0)
# )
# ... replace facet_grid(...) with:
# facet_grid2(Theme ~ ., scales="free_y", space="free_y",
#             switch="y", strip=strip_designs)
```

```{r}
#
# Strategy:
#   - Top 30 terms by FDR per database (top 3 for Hallmark — only 3 significant)
#   - Biologically off-target terms excluded (neuronal, embryonic, EDMD)
#   - Unknown TFT motifs (no TF name) excluded
#   - Remaining terms grouped into biological themes
#   - One dot plot per database, saved individually + combined 2x2
#
# Required input files (same folder as this script):
#   all_go_ORA.csv  |  all_cp.csv  |  hallmark_ORA.csv  |  all_tft.csv
#
# Required packages:
#   install.packages(c("tidyverse","scales","patchwork","ggtext"))
#   install.packages("ggh4x")   # optional — cleaner strip colours
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# ── 1. Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
go_raw  <- read_csv("all_go_ORA.csv",   show_col_types = FALSE)
cp_raw  <- read_csv("all_cp.csv",        show_col_types = FALSE)
hl_raw  <- read_csv("hallmark_ORA.csv",  show_col_types = FALSE)
tft_raw <- read_csv("all_tft.csv",       show_col_types = FALSE)

# Helper: parse "52/923" → numeric ratio
parse_ratio <- function(x) {
  parts <- str_split(x, "/")[[1]]
  as.numeric(parts[1]) / as.numeric(parts[2])
}

prep_df <- function(df, db_label) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      GeneRatio_num  = map_dbl(GeneRatio, parse_ratio),
      neg_log10_padj = -log10(p.adjust),
      DB             = db_label
    )
}

go_df  <- prep_df(go_raw,  "GO")
cp_df  <- prep_df(cp_raw,  "CP")
hl_df  <- prep_df(hl_raw,  "Hallmark")
tft_df <- prep_df(tft_raw, "TFT")

# Terms are the top-30 by FDR with off-target / unknown terms removed.

# ── 3. Join curated labels with actual ORA values ────────────────────────────
join_values <- function(terms_tbl, ora_df) {
  terms_tbl %>%
    left_join(
      ora_df %>% select(Description, FoldEnrichment, p.adjust,
                        Count, GeneRatio_num, neg_log10_padj),
      by = "Description"
    )
}

go_plot  <- join_values(go_terms,  go_df)
cp_plot  <- join_values(cp_terms,  cp_df)
hl_plot  <- join_values(hl_terms,  hl_df)
tft_plot <- join_values(tft_terms, tft_df)

# Quick check
check_missing <- function(df, name) {
  miss <- df %>% filter(is.na(FoldEnrichment)) %>% pull(Description)
  if (length(miss) > 0)
    warning(name, " — unmatched: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
  else
    message(name, ": all ", nrow(df), " terms matched OK")
}
check_missing(go_plot,  "GO")
check_missing(cp_plot,  "CP")
check_missing(hl_plot,  "Hallmark")
check_missing(tft_plot, "TFT")

# ── 4. Factor ordering (within theme: highest FE at top; themes by list order)
order_plot_df <- function(df, theme_order) {
  df %>%
    mutate(Theme = factor(Theme, levels = rev(theme_order))) %>%
    group_by(Theme) %>%
    arrange(Theme, FoldEnrichment) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(Display_Label = factor(Display_Label, levels = unique(Display_Label)))
}

# ── 6. Core dot-plot function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
make_panel <- function(df, title_str) {

  x_max   <- max(df$FoldEnrichment, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.35
  fdr_max <- max(df$neg_log10_padj, na.rm = TRUE)

  ggplot(df, aes(x = FoldEnrichment, y = Display_Label)) +

    # Vertical reference at FE = 1
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.45) +

    # Main dots
    geom_point(aes(size = Count, colour = neg_log10_padj), alpha = 0.88) +

    # Facet by theme, strips on left
    facet_grid(Theme ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +

    # Colour: -log10(FDR)
    scale_colour_gradientn(
      colours  = fdr_pal,
      limits   = c(0, fdr_max),
      name     = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
      guide    = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        barwidth  = unit(4, "cm"),
        barheight = unit(0.4, "cm"),
        frame.colour = "grey50"
      )
    ) +

    # Size: gene count
    scale_size_continuous(
      range  = c(2.5, 9),
      name   = "Gene count",
      guide  = guide_legend(
        title.position = "top",
        nrow = 1,
        override.aes = list(colour = "grey35")
      )
    ) +

    # Axes
    scale_x_continuous(
      name   = "Fold Enrichment",
      limits = c(0.85, x_max),
      breaks = pretty_breaks(n = 4),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.04))
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(name = NULL) +

    labs(title = title_str) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title          = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5,
                                          margin = margin(b = 5)),
      # Strip
      strip.placement     = "outside",
      strip.background    = element_rect(fill = "grey25", colour = NA),
      strip.text.y.left   = element_text(
        angle  = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5,
        size   = 7.5, face = "bold", colour = "white",
        margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, t = 1, b = 1)
      ),
      # Panel
      panel.border        = element_rect(colour = "grey70", fill = NA,
                                          linewidth = 0.45),
      panel.grid.major.y  = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x  = element_line(colour = "grey87",
                                          linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.4),
      panel.grid.minor    = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing       = unit(0.18, "lines"),
      # Axes
      axis.text.y         = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey10"),
      axis.text.x         = element_text(size = 8),
      axis.title.x        = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(t = 5)),
      # Legend
      legend.position     = "bottom",
      legend.box          = "horizontal",
      legend.title        = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.text         = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.margin       = margin(t = 2),
      # Margins
      plot.margin         = margin(t = 6, r = 8, b = 4, l = 4)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
}

# ── 7. Build panels ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
p_go  <- make_panel(go_plot,  "Gene Ontology (BP + MF + CC)")
p_cp  <- make_panel(cp_plot,  "Canonical Pathways (KEGG / Reactome / WikiPathways / PID)")
p_hl  <- make_panel(hl_plot,  "MSigDB Hallmark\n(3 significant terms at FDR < 0.05)")
p_tft <- make_panel(tft_plot, "Transcription Factor Targets (TFT)")

# ── 8. Apply per-strip theme colours via grob editing ────────────────────────
colour_strips <- function(p, col_map) {
  library(grid)
  gt         <- ggplotGrob(p)
  strip_idx  <- which(grepl("^strip-l", gt$layout$name))
  theme_lvls <- levels(p$data$Theme)  # already reversed

  for (i in seq_along(strip_idx)) {
    # grobs run top→bottom; factor levels run bottom→top → map from end
    tn  <- theme_lvls[length(theme_lvls) - i + 1]
    col <- col_map[[tn]]
    if (!is.null(col)) {
      sg <- gt$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]]
      sg$grobs[[1]]$children[[1]]$gp$fill <- col   # bg rect
      sg$grobs[[1]]$children[[2]]$gp$col  <- "white" # text
      gt$grobs[[strip_idx[i]]] <- sg
    }
  }
  gt
}

# ── 9. Auto-height save helper ────────────────────────────────────────────────
save_panel <- function(p, col_map, stem, width = 8.5, pts_per_row = 0.27, min_h = 3.5) {

  n_rows <- nrow(p$data)
  n_themes <- n_distinct(p$data$Theme)
  h <- max(min_h, n_rows * pts_per_row + n_themes * 0.25 + 2.5)

  # Plain (always works)
  ggsave(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), p,
         width = width, height = h, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(paste0(stem, ".png"), p,
         width = width, height = h, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  message("Saved: ", stem, ".pdf / .png  (", round(h, 1), "in tall)")

  # Coloured-strip version
  tryCatch({
    gt <- colour_strips(p, col_map)

    pdf(paste0(stem, "_col.pdf"), width = width, height = h)
    grid::grid.draw(gt)
    dev.off()

    png(paste0(stem, "_col.png"),
        width = width, height = h, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
    grid::grid.draw(gt)
    dev.off()

    message("Saved: ", stem, "_col.pdf / .png  (coloured strips)")
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Strip colour edit failed for ", stem, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    message("Tip: install ggh4x for a more reliable alternative.")
  })
}

message("\n--- Saving individual panels ---")
save_panel(p_go,  go_strip_cols,  "ORA_GO_top30")
save_panel(p_cp,  cp_strip_cols,  "ORA_CP_top30")
save_panel(p_hl,  hl_strip_cols,  "ORA_Hallmark_top30",  width = 6, min_h = 2.5)
save_panel(p_tft, tft_strip_cols, "ORA_TFT_top30")

      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30", hjust = 0,
                                    margin = margin(b = 6)),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey45", hjust = 0,
                                    margin = margin(t = 6))
    )
  )

ggsave("ORA_4panel_top30.pdf", combined,
       width = 20, height = 26, units = "in", device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave("ORA_4panel_top30.png", combined,
       width = 20, height = 26, units = "in", dpi = 180, bg = "white")
message("Saved: ORA_4panel_top30.pdf / .png")

# ── 11. ggh4x alternative (cleaner strip colours) ────────────────────────────

message("\nAll done.")
```
